title: Access modifiers and why `private` is the sensible default

videos.script: Every field so far could be read and changed by anyone. This lesson is about saying who may. {{levels}} Java has four answers. Public: anyone. Protected: the package, and subclasses. No word at all: the package. Private: this class and nothing else. The compiler enforces all four, and its messages say which one you hit. {{loan}} Then the reason it matters. A loan may be renewed twice. With an open field, any line anywhere can set the count back to zero, or to seven. With a private field, the only way in is the method that checks. {{files}} Last, the rule about files. One public class per file, named after it. Other classes may share the file, as long as they are not public. By the end you can choose a modifier on purpose, and you start from private.
